- IT Provisioning team owner: it-provisioning@redwood.internal (SLA owner).
- Escalation: if provisioning misses SLA, hiring manager escalates to People Ops partner and the onboarding program lead.

Benefits and perks signposting (what to expect in week 0–2)
- Benefits enrollment window opens on Day 1 and remains for 30 days. People Ops sends reminders on days 3, 10, and 20.
- Stipends (home-office, learning): auto-eligible after payroll activation; request through internal finance form.
- Parental and caregiver policies summarized with links in the LMS module.

Special cases and exceptions
- Remote-first hires across APAC/EU: tax and benefits packaging will differ; People Ops will provide a jurisdiction-specific packet within 48 hours of start.
- Senior hires (Director and above): many provisioning steps are manual (exec laptop prep, additional security briefings) — onboarding lead will create a bespoke checklist.

Onboarding feedback and metrics (how we measure success)
- Primary metrics: time-to-first-PR, 30-day self-reported readiness, manager 30-day rating (1–5).
- Target goals: 75% of cohorts hit time-to-first-PR within 21 days; average manager 30-day rating >= 4.0.
- Monthly retrospective: People Ops runs a 60-minute cohort retro and submits a short improvement plan.

Security & compliance requirements during onboarding
- All new joiners must complete the Secure SDL course within 7 days.
- MFA must be enabled on all accounts before any write-level repo access is granted.
- Contractors must sign the Contractor Data Protection Addendum before being granted access to internal datasets.",

Purpose: This document codifies a compact, repeatable on-call handoff sequence, a lightweight runbook retirement lifecycle, and an opinionated set of templates and automation snippets for keeping the status page and customer communications accurate during incidents. It is intended for first responders, on-call leads, incident commanders, and the SRE engineers who maintain runbooks.

Scope: Applies to Redwood-hosted services, Dedicated control plane components, and customer-facing public APIs. Private deployments should mirror the same approach unless constrained by customer confidentiality agreements.

Quick reference (single-page)

- Primary SLOs: 99.95% p99 availability monthly for API gateway; latency SLO: 95% < 200ms for metadata endpoints.
- Alert thresholds: Error rate > 0.5% for 5m (P1 candidate); p95 latency increase > 3x baseline for 5m (P2 candidate).
- Escalation: Pager -> Team on-call -> On-call lead -> Incident commander.

Customer notification templates (email)
-------------------------------------
Subject: Redwood service incident (INC-2028-042) — summary and next steps

Body:
Hello <CustomerName>,

We are currently investigating an incident affecting Redwood inference in the <region>. Some requests may return errors or experience increased latency. Our engineers have identified a contributing factor and are actively mitigating. We will provide the next update by <time>. If this incident is impacting production-critical workflows, please reply to this email or contact your CSM directly at <CSM Email>.

We apologize for the disruption.
— Redwood Operations

Runbook: immediate checklist (first 30 minutes)
------------------------------------------------
1) Acknowledge on pager and post to #oncall with brief: "ACK INC-xxxx: scope, initial hypothesis, first mitigation action".
2) Confirm incident ID and create incident timeline entry (inc-db or incident-tracker).
3) Run scope commands:
   - curl -sS https://api.redwood.io/health || echo failure
   - kubectl -n runtime get pods --selector=app=serving-runtime -o wide
   - redis-cli HGETALL kv:cache:stats
4) If CPU/GPU queue depth > 85%: trigger horizontal scaling playbook (scaling script: infra/scale-dedicated.sh --burst)
5) If recent deploy within 30 minutes: rollback canary via deploy tool (ci/rollback --tag <previous>).
6) Start a live timeline and attach logs (s3://inc-logs/INC-xxxx).

Postmortem & RCA process (short)
--------------------------------
- Owner: service team. Due within 7 business days for Sev1+, 14 days for Sev2.
- Template to include: incident summary, timeline (minute-granular), root cause, contributing factors, corrective actions (owner + due date), and verification plan.
- Publish in Confluence under /incidents with tag incident-YYYY-MM-DD and link to incident artifacts.",

Escalation matrix & responsibilities
-----------------------------------
- First responder (on-call SRE): owns bridge, initial triage, and the first status page update.
- Serving runtime lead: accountable for KV cache remediation steps and kernel-level diagnostics.
- Platform on-call: executes traffic routing overrides and autoscaler configuration.
- Customer Success on-call: drafts customer notices for affected customers and coordinates targeted DMs.
- Incident commander: assigned if incident meets P1 criteria or crosses teams; owns postmortem and executive updates.

Runbook commands and snippets
---------------------------
- Identify nodes with prefix mismatches:
  - kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=kvcache -o json | jq '.items[] | {name:.metadata.name, podIP:.status.podIP}'
  - curl -s http://kvcache-<pod>/internal/metrics | grep kv_prefix_mismatch_total

- Restart kvcache on a node safely (cordon & restart):
  - kubectl -n inference cordon <node-name>
  - kubectl -n inference delete pod <kvcache-pod> --grace-period=30
  - kubectl -n inference uncordon <node-name>

- Route override (example):
  - curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ROUTE_ADMIN_TOKEN' \n    -d '{"route":"cpu-infer","pct":100,"ttl":"5m"}' https://routing.redwood.internal/v1/override

- Collect sample traces quickly and upload to evidence bucket:
  - go-run collect-traces --ids "$(cat sample-ids.txt)" --out s3://redwood-evidence/gameday/kvcorrupt/$(date +%F_%T).tgz",

Content: Overview

Purpose: This document codifies a compact, repeatable on-call handoff sequence, a lightweight runbook retirement lifecycle, and an opinionated set of templates and automation snippets for keeping the status page and customer communications accurate during incidents. It is intended for first responders, on-call leads, incident commanders, and the SRE engineers who maintain runbooks.

Scope: Applies to Redwood-hosted services, Dedicated control plane components, and customer-facing public APIs. Private deployments should mirror the same approach unless constrained by customer confidentiality agreements.

Quick reference (single-page)

- Primary SLOs: 99.95% p99 availability monthly for API gateway; latency SLO: 95% < 200ms for metadata endpoints.
- Alert thresholds: Error rate > 0.5% for 5m (P1 candidate); p95 latency increase > 3x baseline for 5m (P2 candidate).
- Escalation: Pager -> Team on-call -> On-call lead -> Incident commander.

Incident severity definitions

- Symptom: Progressive P95 latency increase (SLO class: High)\

Escalation matrix & responsibilities
-----------------------------------
- First responder (on-call SRE): owns bridge, initial triage, and the first status page update.

Runbook commands and snippets

- Identify nodes with prefix mismatches:
  - kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=kvcache -o json | jq '.items[] | {name:.metadata.name, podIP:.status.podIP}'

- Restart kvcache on a node safely (cordon & restart):
  - kubectl -n inference cordon <node-name>
  - kubectl -n inference delete pod <kvcache-pod> --grace-period=30
  - kubectl -n inference uncordon <node-name>

  - go-run collect-traces --ids "$(cat sample-ids.txt)" --out s3://redwood-evidence/gameday/kvcorrupt/$(date +%F_%T).tgz

  "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: SDK local prefetch, mirroring, and cache-encoder playbook\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/confluence\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates/sdk-local-prefetch-mirroring-and-cache-encoder-playbook-2026.json\nConnector: confluence\nWorkspace: eng-developer-experience\n\n3600 (default) - how long local cached entries remain valid\\n- max_cache_size_mb: 50 - per-client disk budget for encoded caches\\n- batch_window_ms: 20 - grouping interval for bundler before sending to runtime\\n- max_prefetch_parallel: 4 - cap parallel prefetch jobs per client\\n- sample_rate_mirror: 0.01 - default mirror sampling for production\\n- eviction_policy: lru | time_based - default lru\\n\\nSLOs and developer expectations for sandbox use:\\n- Prefetch latency (on-cache-hit): < 25ms additional overhead to request path.\\n- Cache hit rate goal for templated workflows: >= 40% for first 60s of activity.\\n- Mirror telemetry lag: < 5s end-to-end into staging traces.\\n- Safety: mirror sampling must never exceed bucketed privacy budget and must be manually enabled for new customers.\\n\\nTemplates included (quickstart artifacts):\\n1) response-bundler-template (JavaScript): an express middleware that aggregates multiple client prompts into a bundled multi-request for lower token cost and controlled latency.\\n2) mirror-proxy-template (Go): lightweight HTTP reverse proxy with deterministic sampling, header-masking, and spike-protection circuit breaker.\\n3) encoder-cli-template (Python): build/inspect/rehydrate encoded cache blobs with validation hooks and size reporting.\\n\\nDeployment and rollout checklist (developer-to-production):\\n1. Tracing: attach request-level traces to canary samples.
Logs: structured audit events for start/step/fail/rollback with controller run_id.
Synthetic checks: small harness that hits both new and baseline variants in parallel for golden prompts.
Dashboards: per-rollout timeline with gate status, metric deltas, and decision timestamps.

Objective: Produce a supported-versions matrix that explicitly defines allowed version skew and behavioral contracts between runtime, API, SDKs, and console; deliver a prototype orchestrator that runs preflight validations, performs canary cohort promotions, and executes safe rollbacks based on SLO and functional checks.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Compatibility map document completed and reviewed by Runtime, API, SDK, and Console leads
  - Allowed version skew rules defined for each surface and encoded as machine-readable policies
  - Prototype silent-upgrade orchestrator can run a staged upgrade: canary (5%), ramp (25%), full rollout with automated rollback on defined failure signals
  - Preflight suite of compatibility tests (contract, end-to-end smoke, KV-cache replay) integrated into orchestrator and passing in CI for target minor-version pairs
  - Runbook and rollback playbook documented and linked from Console release page
  - Small-scale private deployment upgrade executed in staging with no customer-facing errors and post-upgrade metrics within SLOs

## Rollout Gates

- Preflight: contract checks (OpenAPI/protobuf), semantic schema diffs, SDK surface diff reports
  - Performance smoke: 95th percentile token latency within 1.5x baseline for a representative workload
  - Behavioral smoke: 20 canonical prompt/eval set pass rate within 98% of baseline
  - Observability: tracing and token-level cost events are present and mapped to new runtime version
  - Canary cohort: 5% of traffic for 2 hours with anomaly detection (error rate, latency, quality metrics), manual approval if anomalies are ambiguous
  - Ramp gate: automatic step-up to 25% then 100% if no gate breaches; each step requires at least 30 minutes of stable telemetry
  - Rollback triggers: sustained error rate > 0.5% above baseline for 5 minutes OR quality regression > 2% on canonical evals OR severe latency spike beyond configured SLO breach

  "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Cascade Batch Sherpa: workload-aware batching advisor with staged safe-apply\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/linear\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-121001-cascade-batch-sherpa.json\nConnector: linear\nWorkspace: engineering\nProject: cost-optimization\nTeam: engineering\n\nator can perform shadow apply, 1% canary, and auto-rollback if any telemetry threshold is breached, 4) Integration tests and a dry-run mode exist and show no change to live traffic before canary, 5) Documentation and runtime-1.26 release notes include behavioral description and telemetry queries.\n\nImplementation Notes: Design: 1) Workload profiler aggregates per-route metrics (seq_len distribution, arrival inter-arrival time, token-per-request, KV-hit ratio) into a compact fingerprint (stable hash + histograms). 2) Heuristic scoring engine maps fingerprints to a Pareto front of candidate configs using conservative cost/latency trade-off rules derived from offline microbenchmarks. 3) Continuous tuner runs a low-frequency hill-climb (or Bayesian bandit with safety margin) to propose parameter deltas that are shadow-tested before canary. 4) Safe-apply orchestration: shadow apply -> observe internal metrics (latency P50/P95/P99, tail CPU/GPU utilization, OOMs, error rate) -> canary rollout 1% -> ramp with backoff up to configured cap. The update will be scoped to runtime routing, autoscale, and release pipelines (hosted + dedicated).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Staged rollback contracts: For any runtime change affecting routing or model variant selection, a 3-stage rollout (canary 1%, regional ramp, global ramp) must be defined with explicit SLO thresholds; if 95th- or 99th-percentile latency or error-rate exceeds threshold for 5m in the canary stage, automated rollback triggers within 2m.
  - Synthetic canary harness: Implement a CI job that runs synthetic traffic (tail-latency and correctness prompts) against canary instances for every release; canary tests produce a pass/fail signal in CI and must be green before proceeding to ramp stage.
  - Telemetry gates: Dashboards (per-route, per-model) including latency P50/P95/P99, error-rate, token-cost delta, and KV-cache hit-rate must be auto-generated and declared green in the release checklist; ownership assigned to runtime-observability (ENG-22488).
  - Runbook integration: Rollback steps and escalation targets (SRE pager list, on-call runbook link) must be embedded in PRD; runbook must include isolation steps, diagnostic queries, and rollout-shepherd instructions for traffic shepherding and traffic pinning.
  - Test coverage: Add automated integration tests that simulate regional capacity loss and validate that staged rollback and fallback to compatible model variant works within acceptance latency bounds.
  - Audit & traceability: Every release that used staged rollback contracts must include a short post-release verification note with links to dashboards and Canary CI results; the PRD mandates storage of these artifacts for 90 days.

SLOs and developer expectations for sandbox use:

- Cache hit rate goal for templated workflows: >= 40% for first 60s of activity.

- Safety: mirror sampling must never exceed bucketed privacy budget and must be manually enabled for new customers.

Templates included (quickstart artifacts):

Deployment and rollout checklist (developer-to-production):
1. Local dev: enable prefetch agent with cache_ttl_seconds reduced to 60 to avoid stale data.
2. Integration test: run mirror-proxy with --sample-rate 1.0 against a staging model, ingest traces into observability sandbox.
3. Canary: enable mirror sampling 1% in production for 24 hours, monitor quality regressions and error spikes.
4. Gradual roll: increment sample rate and on-device prefetch within 1–2 week windows, maintain runbook-held abort criteria.

Abort criteria and runbook triggers:
- If staging mirrored requests show a completion divergence rate > 4% for gold prompt-set, rollback mirror and open triage.

Canary schedule defaults: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% with wait windows 10m, 20m, 30m, 1h (configurable).

Gates: We will provide a set of preconfigured gates and allow custom metric expressions:
- Latency Gate: p95 increase <= 15% relative to baseline over gate window (default 15m).
- Error Gate: request 5xx rate <= baseline + 0.2% absolute (sliding 15m).
- Decode Failure Gate: any spike > 3x baseline triggers immediate fail.
- Quality Gate: evaluated by running 200 golden prompts against new and baseline models and checking BLEU/ROUGE/semantic-similarity delta; fail if quality drops > configured delta (default 2%).
- Resource Gate: GPU memory pressure > 80% sustained for 5m causes pause.
Gate evaluation semantics: each gate returns pass/warn/fail. A single fail triggers auto-rollback when automation is enabled. Warns pause ramp and require manual approval to continue.

Instrumentation: Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, token generation time, 5xx counts, decode-fail counts, throughput, GPU memory/SM utilization.
Tracing: attach request-level traces to canary samples.
Logs: structured audit events for start/step/fail/rollback with controller run_id.
Synthetic checks: small harness that hits both new and baseline variants in parallel for golden prompts.
Dashboards: per-rollout timeline with gate status, metric deltas, and decision timestamps.

Implementation Notes: Design: 1) Workload profiler aggregates per-route metrics (seq_len distribution, arrival inter-arrival time, token-per-request, KV-hit ratio) into a compact fingerprint (stable hash + histograms). 2) Heuristic scoring engine maps fingerprints to a Pareto front of candidate configs using conservative cost/latency trade-off rules derived from offline microbenchmarks. 3) Continuous tuner runs a low-frequency hill-climb (or Bayesian bandit with safety margin) to propose parameter deltas that are shadow-tested before canary. 4) Safe-apply orchestration: shadow apply -> observe internal metrics (latency P50/P95/P99, tail CPU/GPU utilization, OOMs, error rate) -> canary rollout 1% -> ramp with backoff up to configured cap. - cost_delta_query: SELECT sum(tokens)*unit_cost FROM token_usage WHERE route=$route AND after_config=true - before_config=true

  - error_rate: SELECT count(status>=500)/count(*) FROM requests WHERE route=$route AND window=5m
  - kv_hit_rate: SELECT sum(kv_hits)/sum(kv_lookups) FROM kv_metrics WHERE route=$route AND window=1h

Description: Build a drift-aware progressive delivery framework for runtime upgrades and model version promotions. Goals: minimize user-visible regressions, enforce LTS compatibility rules, reduce manual toil for canaries and rollbacks, and introduce automated fallback paths when runtime or model drift is detected. The scope covers: - version compatibility checks (binary, weights, KV cache schema) - staged traffic ramps with adaptive gates driven by telemetry - canary cohorts, shadowing and mirrored traffic modes - feature-flag driven opt-in/out and emergency kill-switch - automatic rollback policies tied to SLO/quality gates - tooling to declare LTS channels and safe upgrade windows

Rollout Plan Summary: 1) Preflight: run compatibility checks and smoke-tests on preprod cluster; 2) Canary: route 0.5% traffic to canary cohort for 10 minutes with full tracing; 3) Adaptive ramp: increase to 5%, 20%, 50% using telemetry gates (latency p95, error rate, quality delta); 4) Final cutover: promote to LTS channel if all gates green; 5) Auto-rollback: trigger immediate fallback if any critical gate trips; 6) Post-mortem: automated artifact collection and release note generation.

- Immediate rollback: redwoodctl rollback --deployment $DEPLOY_ID --target-model $PREVIOUS_MODEL --max-wait 30m --evidence /tmp/pf.json

guardrails:

3600 (default) - how long local cached entries remain valid
- max_cache_size_mb: 50 - per-client disk budget for encoded caches
- batch_window_ms: 20 - grouping interval for bundler before sending to runtime
- max_prefetch_parallel: 4 - cap parallel prefetch jobs per client
- sample_rate_mirror: 0.01 - default mirror sampling for production
- eviction_policy: lru | time_based - default lru

SLOs and developer expectations for sandbox use:
- Prefetch latency (on-cache-hit): < 25ms additional overhead to request path.
- Cache hit rate goal for templated workflows: >= 40% for first 60s of activity.
- Mirror telemetry lag: < 5s end-to-end into staging traces.
- Safety: mirror sampling must never exceed bucketed privacy budget and must be manually enabled for new customers.

Templates included (quickstart artifacts):
1) response-bundler-template (JavaScript): an express middleware that aggregates multiple client prompts into a bundled multi-request for lower token cost and controlled latency.
2) mirror-proxy-template (Go): lightweight HTTP reverse proxy with deterministic sampling, header-masking, and spike-protection circuit breaker.
3) encoder-cli-template (Python): build/inspect/rehydrate encoded cache blobs with validation hooks and size reporting.

Deployment and rollout checklist (developer-to-production):
1. Local dev: enable prefetch agent with cache_ttl_seconds reduced to 60 to avoid stale data.
2. Integration test: run mirror-proxy with --sample-rate 1.0 against a staging model, ingest traces into observability sandbox.
3. Canary: enable mirror sampling 1% in production for 24 hours, monitor quality regressions and error spikes.
4. Gradual roll: increment sample rate and on-device prefetch within 1–2 week windows, maintain runbook-held abort criteria.

Abort criteria and runbook triggers:
- If staging mirrored requests show a completion divergence rate > 4% for gold prompt-set, rollback mirror and open triage.

Compatibility Testing: We will add a 'compat-suite' matrix that runs against every candidate release: SDK smoke tests, API contract tests (golden request/response fixtures), on-disk migration tests, and end-to-end performance regression checks. The matrix runs on combinations of previous two MAJOR versions and the new candidate.

Rollout Gates: Gates for progressive rollout: 1) Unit/integration checks pass 2) Contract tests pass against previous major fixtures 3) Canary: 5% traffic for 24h with elevated telemetry 4) Gradual increase to 25% for 48h 5) Production ramp to 100% unless predefined error/latency thresholds breach. Gate metrics: error_rate (>=5xx) delta > 0.5% absolute, p95 latency regression > 20%, token loss or generation drift flagged by eval set regressions.

Rollback Triggers: Automatic rollback if any gate metric breaches AND absolute impact exceeds our safety threshold (see rollout_gates). Manual rollback can be triggered by SRE/Oncall for severe customer-visible failures. Rollbacks must have a postmortem linked and a follow-up fix ticket.

Upgrade Tooling: Deliverables: 1) 'rwu' CLI (redwood-upgrade) to validate binary compatibility and run preflight checks on Dedicated/Private clusters. 2) Control-plane API endpoints to orchestrate canary percentages and schedule automated rollbacks. 3) Migration helpers (one-shot jobs) for on-disk KV schema upgrades, with dry-run mode and verification checks.

Cli Preflight Checks: rwu preflight will verify: cluster health, schema versions, pinned model compatibility, available disk and GPU resources, and run contract self-test against a local golden fixture. It returns structured exit codes and human-readable guidance for remediation.

Body: Overview:

Purpose
This playbook defines a repeatable, lightweight embedded onboarding pattern tailored for hires joining Product and Platform teams at Redwood. It aligns role ramp expectations, tooling access timelines, manager and mentor responsibilities, and a standardized handover template so new joiners reach measurable impact faster while minimizing operational friction.

Scope
- Applies to full-time ICs (levels IC1–IC5) and engineering managers joining Product, Platform, and Core infra teams.
- Not a replacement for team-specific PRDs or technical deep dives; it supplements those with operational and people processes.

Owners and Escalation
- Playbook owner: People Ops (Anika Rao).
- Tier 1 operational owner for tooling: Platform Operations (SRE) team.
- Escalation: raise to People Ops if provisioning SLAs exceed thresholds (see Access SLA section).

Principles
1) Predictable first 30 days: reduce variability across teams with a 0–30 day milestone map.
2) Role-tailored but consistent: core checkpoints are uniform; technical ramp content varies by team.
3) Manager-driven outcomes, mentor-supported development: managers set goals; mentors help reduce cognitive overhead.
4) Automated, auditable provisioning: avoid ad-hoc access requests.

Quick Start (for hiring manager)
1. Fill the Embedded Onboarding Form (People Ops template) at offer acceptance.
2. Assign a primary mentor and a technical buddy before Day 0.
3. Confirm required tool access and sensitive systems with Platform Ops within 48 hours.
4. Publish the 90-day success criteria in the team’s workspace.

Preboarding Checklist (to complete before Day 0)
- Offer paperwork processed and payroll setup confirmed.
- Laptop chosen and procurement ticket created (include required GPU/VM specs if applicable).
- Identity (SSO) account created with base groups: contributor, slack, okta.
- Read-ahead packet sent (team charter, current roadmap, recent design reviews).
- First-week calendar blocks created: 1:1s

possible.

Scope and audience:
- Primary: people-ops + hiring manager + assigned buddy/mentor.
- Roles: ICs across engineering, product, and applied ML (adaptable templates).
- Not a replacement for manager 1:1s; complements existing 30-60-90 templates.

Envelope contents (what gets sent pre-Day 1):
1) Quick-start checklist (1 page): account access, tooling, required trainings (sensitive data, security), calendar invites for buddy + first-week sync.
2) Role micro-goals: 3 measurable outcomes for 30d, 60d, 120d. Each outcome has an owner (often the hire) and a success metric.
3) Shadow slot schedule: 6 half-day cross-functional shadow blocks in first 60 days (product review, infra oncall walkthrough, sre runbook tour, cs handoff meeting, release cadence sync, qa/validation demo). Template calendar invites included.
4) Mentor/buddy rotation plan: 2-week rotation cadence where the hire pairs with a different mentor each week for focused 90-minute sessions (architecture, product context, release flow, codebase orientation).
5) Early signals dashboard: list of observable signals people-ops + manager track weekly (merged PRs, first customer touch, telemetry dashboards visited, ticket churn).
6) Rapid remediation ladder: if signal thresholds aren’t met by day 30/60, this prescribes actions: re-assess, shadow intensification, 1:1 skill coach, or role-scope adjustment.
7) Lightweight interview probe bank: 6-8 role-specific quick probes managers can use to confirm mid-onboard progress (behavioral + technical).
8) Templates: intro email to team, buddy intro, manager 7-day check-in script, manager 30-day calibration rubric.

regular employees and contractors transitioning back to Redwood after >30 days away, and to internal transfers that include a substantive tooling or competency change (e.g., moving into infra, SRE, data, or manager tracks). Does not replace standard new-hire onboarding; it augments it for reentry scenarios.

Principles
- Employee-centered: prioritize psychological safety, clear expectations, and flexible timing.
- Measured ramp: use explicit 30/60/90 milestones with objective signals of progress.
- Role-aware provisioning: grant minimum required access initially, expand after verification.
- Manager + People Ops partnership: shared accountability for timelines and outcomes.

Eligibility and Typical Use Cases
- Parental return (12–26 weeks leave)
- Sabbatical or extended unpaid leave (1–12 months)
- Medical leave followed by phased reentry
- External secondments or long-term project assignments returning to a different team
- Internal role changes that require cross-skilling (IC -> manager, IC -> infra/data/product)

Reentry Pathways (choose one primary pathway)
1) Standard Phased Return (typical parental/sabbatical): 30/60/90 ramp, benefits maintained, toolkit reprovisioned within SLAs.
2) Phased + Upskill (return + new competencies): same as Standard + structured reskilling curriculum and mentor pairing.
3) Role Transition Reboard (internal transfer): transfer checklist + dedicated onboarding buddy + skills validation prior to full access.

Operational SLAs (targets)
- Primary communication acknowledged by manager & People Ops: 2 business days.
- Minimum workspace access (email, Slack, Confluence read): 1 business day after reactivation.
- Developer-level access (GitHub, CI, secrets read): within 3 business days after manager approval.
- Elevated system access (PagerDuty, production consoles): verified gating and granted within 5 business days after training verification.

## Purpose and boundary

Runtime Diagnostics turns runtime degradation into fast, reproducible, evidence-backed findings and promotes validated findings into controls that prevent or shorten recurrence. The team supports SRE during live incidents and Runtime during deep investigation. SRE remains incident commander and mitigation authority; Runtime remains owner of runtime code and fixes; Runtime Diagnostics owns investigation quality, artifacts, validation discipline, and the finding-to-control workflow. Accept work from: an active incident/IC, an SLO or release-gate breach, a repeated Support or Customer Success pattern, a Runtime escalation, or a planned failover/release validation.

Every case starts with one intake record containing:

- case and incident/change IDs; requester; assigned diagnostics lead; IC or service owner;
- severity and customer impact; affected tier, tenant cohort, route, model/runtime version, region, and time window;
- observed versus expected behavior and the decision the investigation must unblock;
- links to alerts, dashboards, request/trace IDs, recent deploys and configuration changes;
- data classification, residency, retention, and access constraints.

For a live incident, attach the case to the incident record and acknowledge through the IC. Diagnostics does not create a competing command channel. Missing fields never delay urgent evidence capture; the lead backfills them in the timeline.

Established: 2026-07-27  
Operating horizon: first 90 days

## Mission

Make Redwood Inference's customer-facing runtime predictable, diagnosable, and recoverable by turning availability and latency objectives, runtime failure modes, incident evidence, regional resilience, and release risk into shared engineering controls with named owners and measurable validation.

- Define reliability policy and reusable service contracts: SLI/SLO semantics, error-budget controls, failure-mode taxonomy, diagnostic acceptance criteria, and ownership mappings.

# Runtime Diagnostics Team Operating Plan

Effective: 2026-07-27  
Parent: Reliability Engineering

## Purpose and boundary

Runtime Diagnostics turns runtime degradation into fast, reproducible, evidence-backed findings and promotes validated findings into controls that prevent or shorten recurrence. The team supports SRE during live incidents and Runtime during deep investigation. SRE remains incident commander and mitigation authority; Runtime remains owner of runtime code and fixes; Runtime Diagnostics owns investigation quality, artifacts, validation discipline, and the finding-to-control workflow. [workspace_594675f335939dce30b8f76a, `/knowledge/departments/reliability-engineering/charter.md`]

## 1. Intake

Accept work from: an active incident/IC, an SLO or release-gate breach, a repeated Support or Customer Success pattern, a Runtime escalation, or a planned failover/release validation.

Every case starts with one intake record containing:

- case and incident/change IDs; requester; assigned diagnostics lead; IC or service owner;
- severity and customer impact; affected tier, tenant cohort, route, model/runtime version, region, and time window;
- observed versus expected behavior and the decision the investigation must unblock;
- links to alerts, dashboards, request/trace IDs, recent deploys and configuration changes;
- data classification, residency, retention, and access constraints.

For a live incident, attach the case to the incident record and acknowledge through the IC. Diagnostics does not create a competing command channel. Missing fields never delay urgent evidence capture; the lead backfills them in the timeline.

- If mitigation requires changes to kernel binaries or driver-level config.

Post-experiment steps and documentation
1) Collate artifacts and fill the experiment summary template (attach to ticket).
2) If mitigation is successful and low-risk, create a rollout PR with canary matrix and perf gates.
3) If unresolved, escalate to a dedicated investigation and consider a small-scale perf-capture party (day-long).

Ownership and contacts
- Runtime on-call: runtime-oncall@redwood.example.com
- Kernel scheduling primary: Marcus Liu (marcus@redwood.example.com)
- Observability / telemetry: Jordan Reyes (jordan@redwood.example.com)

## Runbook Extracts

- If Full lane saturation > 85% for >3m: escalate to on-call, temporarily increase Reduced lane tokens by 20% if error budget allows

  - If cross-region egress increases >5x baseline: trigger cost review and consider temporary regional scaling

knowledge/departments/reliability-engineering/charter.md:6:## Mission
knowledge/departments/reliability-engineering/charter.md:8:Make Redwood Inference's customer-facing runtime predictable, diagnosable, and recoverable by turning availability and latency objectives, runtime failure modes, incident evidence, regional resilience, and release risk into shared engineering controls with named owners and measurable validation.
knowledge/departments/reliability-engineering/charter.md:10:## Responsibilities
knowledge/departments/reliability-engineering/charter.md:13:- Lead cross-service reliability programs for incident reduction, graceful degradation, regional resilience, and SLO-coupled release safety.
knowledge/departments/reliability-engineering/charter.md:14:- Maintain the common investigation system: intake standards, required metrics/traces/logs/config and deploy context, reproducible timelines, hypothesis and validation records, and promotion of confirmed findings into runbooks, alerts, tests, and design constraints.
knowledge/departments/reliability-engineering/charter.md:15:- Coordinate game days and production-readiness validation for failover, rollback, load shedding, and high-risk runtime releases; track systemic remediation to verified closure.
knowledge/departments/reliability-engineering/charter.md:16:- Produce auditable availability evidence for Product, Customer Success, and Support, while keeping contractual commitments and external communications with their accountable business owners.
knowledge/departments/reliability-engineering/charter.md:17:- Measure department outcomes through customer-impact minutes, error-budget burn, detection and mitigation time, repeat-incident rate, rollback/failover validation coverage, and time from confirmed finding to durable control.
knowledge/departments/reliability-engineering/charter.md:19:## Interfaces
knowledge/departments/reliability-engineering/charter.md:21:### Site Reliability Engineering (SRE)
knowledge/departments/reliability-engineering/charter.md:23:SRE retains production on-call, incident command, immediate mitigation authority, service-level SLO stewardship, and operational runbooks. Reliability Engineering supplies cross-service standards, diagnostic tooling, systemic analysis, game-day design, and validated remediation programs. During incidents, SRE commands and restores service; Reliability Engineering embeds as a diagnostics and evidence function and owns cross-incident learning after stabilization. This separation follows Redwood's existing incident-owner and runbook lifecycle model and its SRE/runtime co-shipping model. [dsid_363b6658e9524c3cbadeb4579d4ac7e0, `/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/runbook-curation-and-incident-ownership-guidelines-2025.json`; dsid_57af13fe38eb4113b6e6083f571ecff9, `/knowledge/company/sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/site-reliability-engineering/dependability-compass-cross-team-playmap.json`]
knowledge/departments/reliability-engineering/charter.md:25:### Runtime
knowledge/departments/reliability-engineering/charter.md:27:Runtime retains ownership of runtime architecture, code, performance, compatibility, instrumentation implementation, fallback hooks, and safe changes. Reliability Engineering defines the cross-runtime reliability contract and diagnostic/release acceptance criteria, validates failure behavior with Runtime, and drives systemic follow-through. Runtime is accountable for implementation; Reliability Engineering is accountable for the evidence that a reliability control works across services and regions. [dsid_c465fce74b6f4d418706729e67969285, `/knowledge/company/sources/linear/engineering/ENG-19876-operational-service-contract-and-failure-mode-matrix.json`; dsid_57af13fe38eb4113b6e6083f571ecff9, `/knowledge/company/sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/site-reliability-engineering/dependability-compass-cross-team-playmap.json`]
knowledge/departments/reliability-engineering/charter.md:29:## First-quarter priorities
knowledge/departments/reliability-engineering/charter.md:33:2. **Stand up the incident-to-durable-control loop.** Standardize intake, incident evidence, validation, and review; add recent deploys, config diffs, saturation, affected cohorts, and region/model context to diagnostic collection; require each confirmed systemic finding to become an owned runbook, alert, regression test, release gate, or design constraint. [enterprise_fe444cd990af49b08f34ba5f, `/knowledge/company/project_list.txt`; dsid_363b6658e9524c3cbadeb4579d4ac7e0, `/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/runbook-curation-and-incident-ownership-guidelines-2025.json`]
knowledge/departments/reliability-engineering/charter.md:35:3. **Validate regional failover as a controlled safety system.** Run hosted and dedicated exercises with SRE, Runtime, Routing, and Fleet; verify target capacity, residency constraints, gradual traffic shift, cache warmup, customer-impact signals, stop conditions, rollback, and retained evidence. Convert gaps into owned remediation. [enterprise_fe444cd990af49b08f34ba5f, `/knowledge/company/project_list.txt`; dsid_88d9d5d9a1b746e6ad01cba7bf0da5c4, `/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/eng-infra/runbooks/gpu-pool-drain-and-evacuation-procedure.json`]
knowledge/departments/reliability-engineering/charter.md:37:4. **Make runtime releases SLO-gated and reversible.** Define one release evidence packet and promotion policy for Hosted and Dedicated: preflight, cohort canaries, latency/error/saturation and correctness gates, decision audit trail, automatic abort/rollback, and post-rollback validation. Prioritize integration between rollout control and SLO burn signals. [enterprise_fe444cd990af49b08f34ba5f, `/knowledge/company/project_list.txt`; dsid_62bd575d44e5409abddcf9836f6f8f6a, `/knowledge/company/sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/release-engineering/launch-checklist-dedicated-staged-rollouts.json`]
knowledge/departments/reliability-engineering/charter.md:39:5. **Close the customer-availability evidence loop.** Align tier/region/endpoint SLO views with incident classification, status components, Support/Customer Success handoffs, and post-incident evidence; publish internal dashboards and an auditable method for explaining availability without creating unreviewed contractual promises. [dsid_26fe354d38864e5ca426dabec101045a, `/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/eng-sre/reliability-initiatives/tiered-slo-and-error-budget-program-q1-2026.json`; enterprise_fe444cd990af49b08f34ba5f, `/knowledge/company/project_list.txt`]
knowledge/departments/reliability-engineering/charter.md:41:## Decision rule
knowledge/departments/reliability-engineering/charter.md:43:Reliability Engineering may set shared evidence and validation requirements and pause a planned promotion when a defined gate fails. Production incident command and emergency mitigation remain with SRE; runtime implementation decisions remain with Runtime. Unresolved cross-team risk is escalated to the accountable service owner and department lead with the evidence packet and explicit customer-impact tradeoff.
knowledge/teams/runtime-diagnostics/operating-plan.md:1:# Runtime Diagnostics Team Operating Plan
knowledge/teams/runtime-diagnostics/operating-plan.md:6:## Purpose and boundary
knowledge/teams/runtime-diagnostics/operating-plan.md:8:Runtime Diagnostics turns runtime degradation into fast, reproducible, evidence-backed findings and promotes validated findings into controls that prevent or shorten recurrence. The team supports SRE during live incidents and Runtime during deep investigation. SRE remains incident commander and mitigation authority; Runtime remains owner of runtime code and fixes; Runtime Diagnostics owns investigation quality, artifacts, validation discipline, and the finding-to-control workflow. [workspace_594675f335939dce30b8f76a, `/knowledge/departments/reliability-engineering/charter.md`]
knowledge/teams/runtime-diagnostics/operating-plan.md:10:## 1. Intake
knowledge/teams/runtime-diagnostics/operating-plan.md:12:Accept work from: an active incident/IC, an SLO or release-gate breach, a repeated Support or Customer Success pattern, a Runtime escalation, or a planned failover/release validation.
knowledge/teams/runtime-diagnostics/operating-plan.md:22:For a live incident, attach the case to the incident record and acknowledge through the IC. Diagnostics does not create a competing command channel. Missing fields never delay urgent evidence capture; the lead backfills them in the timeline.
knowledge/teams/runtime-diagnostics/operating-plan.md:24:## 2. Investigation and required artifacts
knowledge/teams/runtime-diagnostics/operating-plan.md:32:5. `traces-logs/` — sampled trace IDs and minimal log slices with timestamps; hash tenant identifiers and exclude raw prompts or PII unless an approved evidence process requires them.
knowledge/teams/runtime-diagnostics/operating-plan.md:34:7. `hypotheses.md` — ranked hypotheses, supporting and contradicting evidence, planned probes, and confidence.
knowledge/teams/runtime-diagnostics/operating-plan.md:37:10. `validation.md` — conclusion, confidence, customer scope, counterfactual/baseline comparison, residual risk, and required durable controls.
knowledge/teams/runtime-diagnostics/operating-plan.md:39:This bundle extends Redwood's published artifact practice—probe manifests, anonymized samples, telemetry snapshots, and decision logs—and the incident standard for timelines, evidence, mitigation records, and owned remediation. [dsid_af125e875c004628a365e906c6d889ea, `/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/root-cause-hypothesis-matrix-and-probe-realignment-2026.json`; dsid_363b6658e9524c3cbadeb4579d4ac7e0, `/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/runbook-curation-and-incident-ownership-guidelines-2025.json`]
knowledge/teams/runtime-diagnostics/operating-plan.md:41:## 3. Investigation method and validation
knowledge/teams/runtime-diagnostics/operating-plan.md:45:3. Rank hypotheses before running probes; record evidence both for and against each.
knowledge/teams/runtime-diagnostics/operating-plan.md:51:- **Validated** when a repeatable probe, controlled reversal, or equivalent causal evidence isolates the mechanism; the mitigation changes the predicted signal; customer-facing recovery is confirmed against baseline/SLO; and the accountable owner reviews the conclusion.
knowledge/teams/runtime-diagnostics/operating-plan.md:53:- **Unresolved** when evidence is insufficient or contradictory. State that explicitly; do not promote the hypothesis as fact.
knowledge/teams/runtime-diagnostics/operating-plan.md:55:Release and failover validation must preserve gate decisions, traffic stages, signal deltas, stop/rollback conditions, and the stable observation window. A failed critical gate is evidence to stop or roll back, not a prompt to weaken the gate during the event. [dsid_62bd575d44e5409abddcf9836f6f8f6a, `/knowledge/company/sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/release-engineering/launch-checklist-dedicated-staged-rollouts.json`; dsid_88d9d5d9a1b746e6ad01cba7bf0da5c4, `/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/eng-infra/runbooks/gpu-pool-drain-and-evacuation-procedure.json`]
knowledge/teams/runtime-diagnostics/operating-plan.md:57:## 4. Escalation
knowledge/teams/runtime-diagnostics/operating-plan.md:59:- **Immediately to the IC/SRE on-call:** worsening customer impact, unexpected blast-radius growth, multi-region symptoms, exhausted rollback path, evidence that a mitigation is harmful, or a customer SLO/release gate crossing. SRE decides live mitigation.
knowledge/teams/runtime-diagnostics/operating-plan.md:60:- **Runtime owner/on-call:** runtime crash/OOM, kernel/compiler/tokenization, batching/scheduling, model-load, KV-cache, output-integrity, or version-compatibility mechanisms.
knowledge/teams/runtime-diagnostics/operating-plan.md:66:If a live investigation has no viable discriminating hypothesis after 30 minutes, broaden the bridge through the IC. If planned probes still fail to explain the event, open a deep-investigation track with an accountable 24-hour checkpoint rather than keeping the incident channel open-ended. [dsid_af125e875c004628a365e906c6d889ea, `/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/root-cause-hypothesis-matrix-and-probe-realignment-2026.json`]
knowledge/teams/runtime-diagnostics/operating-plan.md:68:## 5. Promotion of durable findings
knowledge/teams/runtime-diagnostics/operating-plan.md:70:For every validated P0/P1 mechanism, repeated failure class, or material release/failover gap, open at least one promotion item:
knowledge/teams/runtime-diagnostics/operating-plan.md:75:- a release, SLO, compatibility, or automatic-rollback gate;
knowledge/teams/runtime-diagnostics/operating-plan.md:80:Promotion is complete only when the item links to the case evidence, names an owner and due/review date, includes a verification method, and is exercised or observed successfully. The diagnostics lead records the promotion decision in `validation.md`; the receiving owner accepts it; Runtime Diagnostics verifies closure. Probable or unresolved hypotheses may create experiments, but must not be stored as validated memory. When later evidence changes a durable finding, supersede the earlier memory instead of leaving contradictory guidance.
knowledge/teams/runtime-diagnostics/operating-plan.md:84:## Cadence and measures
knowledge/teams/runtime-diagnostics/operating-plan.md:86:- Daily: active-case review and evidence/owner check.
knowledge/teams/runtime-diagnostics/operating-plan.md:87:- Weekly: Runtime + SRE finding review; accept promotion items and clear ownership.
knowledge/teams/runtime-diagnostics/operating-plan.md:88:- Monthly: sample completed cases for artifact completeness and validation quality.
knowledge/teams/runtime-diagnostics/operating-plan.md:89:- Quarterly: report time to useful hypothesis, time to validated finding, repeat-incident rate, percentage of validated findings promoted and verified, diagnostic coverage of top failure modes, and customer-impact minutes avoided or shortened.

Gates: We will provide a set of preconfigured gates and allow custom metric expressions:
- Latency Gate: p95 increase <= 15% relative to baseline over gate window (default 15m).
- Error Gate: request 5xx rate <= baseline + 0.2% absolute (sliding 15m).
- Decode Failure Gate: any spike > 3x baseline triggers immediate fail.
- Quality Gate: evaluated by running 200 golden prompts against new and baseline models and checking BLEU/ROUGE/semantic-similarity delta; fail if quality drops > configured delta (default 2%).
- Resource Gate: GPU memory pressure > 80% sustained for 5m causes pause.
Gate evaluation semantics: each gate returns pass/warn/fail. A single fail triggers auto-rollback when automation is enabled. Warns pause ramp and require manual approval to continue.

Instrumentation: Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, token generation time, 5xx counts, decode-fail counts, throughput, GPU memory/SM utilization.
Tracing: attach request-level traces to canary samples.
Logs: structured audit events for start/step/fail/rollback with controller run_id.
Synthetic checks: small harness that hits both new and baseline variants in parallel for golden prompts.
Dashboards: per-rollout timeline with gate status, metric deltas, and decision timestamps.

[ ] COM4: Change management packet for regulated customers (if needed)
    - Audit event coverage summary
    - Retention/export statement
    - RBAC overview

Rollback plan (must be executable in <15 minutes)
Principles
- Prefer flag rollback over code rollback.
- Rollback should revert routing behavior first (protect SLOs), then disable promotion actions, then reduce telemetry surface.

Rollback triggers (examples)
- Elevated 429s or sustained queue depth spike in canary stage indicating capacity starvation.
- Routing misassignment across stage partitions or region bleed.
- Gate evaluation instability causing repeated false aborts/holds.
- Telemetry cardinality incident.

Rollback steps (ordered)
[ ] R1: Disable routing_stage_partitioning in prod for affected pools/accounts (or globally if unclear scope).
    - Expected effect: all traffic routes to stable partition/path; staged rollout becomes no-op.

[ ] R2: Disable gate_eval_v1 (if gate system suspected)
    - Expected effect: promotion blocks or reverts to manual-only behavior depending on implementation; confirm with Platform.

[ ] R3: Disable console_timeline (if Console endpoints failing / confusing)
    - Expected effect: hide staged rollout workflow; prevent customer actions.

[ ] R4: Disable emit_stage_tags (if telemetry cardinality issues)
    - Note: dashboards will lose stage breakdown; keep baseline pool dashboards.

[ ] R5: Disable master flag dedicated_staged_rollouts.enabled

[ ] R6: If DB migration issue suspected
    - DO NOT attempt down-migration during incident.
    - Mitigation: feature-flag off + hotfix forward.

[ ] R7: Post-rollback validation
    - Confirm pool-level SLOs returning to baseline (latency, error, saturation).
    - Confirm audit events still emitted for any manual actions taken during incident.

-flag controller API, a traffic-ramp controller integrated with the routing layer, a small state machine service for gate evaluations, predefined gate templates (latency/error/quality/regression), Console UI hooks for visualization, runbook + playbook for manual override, and a demo rollout on an internal non-prod model serving path.

Acceptance Criteria: 1) Canary flow can be started from Console or API and will route 1% of traffic to the new version within 5 minutes.
2) System evaluates gates (p95 latency, 5xx rate, decode-error rate, and quality regression against golden prompts) and emits pass/fail decisions to Console timeline.
3) When any gate fails above configured threshold, the controller executes a rollback action within 30s and records the reason in audit logs.
4) Operators can override automation via Console, pausing or accelerating ramps.
5) Integration tests simulate synthetic traffic and verify auto-rollback triggers for injected faults.
6) Documentation and runbook published in Confluence and linked from Console.

Rollout Plan: Phase A (design & proto, 2 sprints): API and controller prototype; gate templates; unit tests.
Phase B (integration, 2 sprints): integrate with routing layer, Console UI, and metrics pipeline; end-to-end smoke tests.
Phase C (canary on internal model, 1 sprint): run 2 internal rollouts, validate thresholds, observe false-positive rate.
Phase D (limited external customers + docs): opt-in customers on Dedicated + Hosted beta.
Canary schedule defaults: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% with wait windows 10m, 20m, 30m, 1h (configurable).

D (limited external customers + docs): opt-in customers on Dedicated + Hosted beta.
Canary schedule defaults: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% with wait windows 10m, 20m, 30m, 1h (configurable).

Gates: We will provide a set of preconfigured gates and allow custom metric expressions:
- Latency Gate: p95 increase <= 15% relative to baseline over gate window (default 15m).
- Error Gate: request 5xx rate <= baseline + 0.2% absolute (sliding 15m).
- Decode Failure Gate: any spike > 3x baseline triggers immediate fail.
- Quality Gate: evaluated by running 200 golden prompts against new and baseline models and checking BLEU/ROUGE/semantic-similarity delta; fail if quality drops > configured delta (default 2%).
- Resource Gate: GPU memory pressure > 80% sustained for 5m causes pause.
Gate evaluation semantics: each gate returns pass/warn/fail. A single fail triggers auto-rollback when automation is enabled. Warns pause ramp and require manual approval to continue.

Instrumentation: Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, token generation time, 5xx counts, decode-fail counts, throughput, GPU memory/SM utilization.
Tracing: attach request-level traces to canary samples.
Logs: structured audit events for start/step/fail/rollback with controller run_id.
Synthetic checks: small harness that hits both new and baseline variants in parallel for golden prompts.
Dashboards: per-rollout timeline with gate status, metric deltas, and decision timestamps.
PRs and contracts: routing-api PR (github.com/redwood/re-routing/pulls/212), controller proto (github.com/redwood/re-release/pulls/37).

Step-by-step rollout (operator solo flow):
0) Pre-announce: post short note to stakeholder channel with expected window and rollback plan.
1) Canary deploy to 2% routing for 10 minutes. Actions: verify canary health (green) in console, no new 5xx.
2) Run quick smoke script (./scripts/smoke-rollout.sh) against canary: checks = health, simple generation, kv-cache warmup, streaming chunking. Record outputs.
3) If canary passes: expand to 25% over 15 minutes. Observe: latency p95, error rate, token throughput.
4) Midpoint probe at 25%: run longer qps load for 10m using loadkit. Compare telemetry to prebaseline.
5) If stable: full ramp to 100% in two steps (60% -> 100%), pausing 10 minutes between steps. Monitor dashboards actively.

## 4. Escalation

- **Immediately to the IC/SRE on-call:** worsening customer impact, unexpected blast-radius growth, multi-region symptoms, exhausted rollback path, evidence that a mitigation is harmful, or a customer SLO/release gate crossing. SRE decides live mitigation.
- **Runtime owner/on-call:** runtime crash/OOM, kernel/compiler/tokenization, batching/scheduling, model-load, KV-cache, output-integrity, or version-compatibility mechanisms.
- **Routing/Fleet/Platform:** traffic policy, failover, capacity, quota, GPU pool, control-plane, or regional-health mechanisms.
- **Observability:** missing, contradictory, high-cardinality, or untrustworthy telemetry that prevents a safe decision.
- **Security/Privacy:** suspected unauthorized access, audit gaps, sensitive prompt/tenant data, residency risk, or forensic preservation needs.
- **Reliability Engineering lead:** a cross-service systemic risk lacks an owner, remediation conflicts with an SLO/customer commitment, or a validated high-severity finding is not accepted into a durable control.

Role: Senior Runtime Reliability Engineer  
Team: Runtime Diagnostics, Reliability Engineering  
Manager: Runtime Diagnostics Engineering Manager  
Member branch: `person/priya-shah-capture-20260727`

## Role and operating boundary

Priya will turn runtime degradation and release-safety signals into fast, reproducible, evidence-backed findings, then help promote validated findings into durable controls such as runbooks, alerts, regression tests, release gates, or design constraints. She supports SRE during live incidents and Runtime during deep investigation. SRE retains incident command and immediate mitigation authority; Runtime retains ownership of runtime code and fixes; Runtime Diagnostics owns investigation quality, evidence artifacts, validation discipline, and finding-to-control follow-through. ## First 30 days: outcomes and evidence of readiness

### Days 1–5 — orient, verify, and make one safe contribution

- Complete access verification and record every remaining entitlement gap with owner, least-privilege scope, and target date.
- Review the Runtime Diagnostics intake, artifact, validation, escalation, and finding-promotion workflow; walk one completed incident from alert through durable control.
- Complete architecture sessions covering request routing, runtime/model versioning, batching/scheduling, GPU and memory behavior, model loading, KV cache, fallback paths, observability, and regional capacity.
- Shadow an SRE incident/on-call workflow and a Runtime/release workflow; document the difference between SRE command, Runtime implementation ownership, and Diagnostics evidence ownership.
- Land a small, low-risk contribution of no more than roughly one workday—for example, a runbook clarification, diagnostic query improvement, missing dashboard link, or test fixture—using normal review.

### Days 6–15 — perform supervised diagnosis

- Serve as diagnostics lead or co-lead on one bounded staging exercise, game day, release-gate investigation, or recent-incident replay.
- Produce a complete case bundle: intake, timeline, environment/config and recent-deploy context, metrics snapshots, minimal traces/logs, hypothesis matrix, probe manifest/results, mitigation record, and validation conclusion.
- Demonstrate safe evidence handling: hash tenant identifiers and exclude raw prompts or PII unless an approved evidence process requires them.
- Present the investigation at the weekly Runtime + SRE finding review, clearly separating observation, hypothesis, validation status, residual risk, and next discriminating test.
- Shadow at least one staged rollout and explain its preflight evidence, canary cohorts, telemetry gates, stop/rollback conditions, decision audit trail, and post-rollback checks.

### Days 16–30 — own a scoped finding-to-control loop

Tags: onboarding, access-provisioning, sla, engineering, runtime-diagnostics

## Summary

Redwood's published engineering onboarding target is to have baseline provisioning (accounts, laptop, and Slack) completed five business days before the start date when requested on time; late-hire baseline requests target completion within two business days after the request. Item-level targets are one business day for Okta/core SSO and security-training assignment, two business days for GitHub organization/repository access and PagerDuty/Datadog alert access, three business days for Redwood Console production-sandbox access, and three to seven business days for a new laptop. Managers should use the expedited channel when an access delay will block Day-1 work.

Internal tools access matrix (standardized defaults)
Note: IT/Provisioning uses this table as the baseline. All requests that deviate must include manager approval and use the Access Exception form.

| System | Full-time Engineer | Product Manager | People Ops | Contractor (long-term) | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| GitHub (org) | write | write | read | write (limited repos) | Engineers get main repo access by default; contractors restricted to a single repo set. |
| Jira (standard) | write | write | admin | write | Product & Eng: access to private product boards; People Ops limited admin for HR-related projects. |
| Redwood Console (prod) | read | read | read | no | Prod write access requires SRE sign-off and approved RBAC ticket. |
| Internal Wiki | write | write | write | read | Editing rights for full-time staff. |
| Payroll/Benefits Portal | no | no | admin | no | People Ops handles benefits enrollment. |
| AWS Console (prod) | no | no | no | no | Accessed via bastion and approved requests; separate infra process. |

Provisioning SLA and ownership
- Target SLA for baseline provisioning (accounts, laptop, Slack): 5 business days before start date. For late hires this becomes 2 business days after request.
- IT Provisioning team owner: it-provisioning@redwood.internal (SLA owner).
- Escalation: if provisioning misses SLA, hiring manager escalates to People Ops partner and the onboarding program lead.
